title: Michael Burry issues blunt warning as he bets against 2 AI favorites
excerpt: Michael Burry has been building short-semiconductor-book lately. I covered his Micron short, his Caterpillar bet, and his SOXX position. His pattern has been...
content_html:
Michael Burry has been building short-semiconductor-book lately. I covered his Micron short, his Caterpillar bet, and his SOXX position. His pattern has been consistent.

He first identifies a narrative the market treats as infallible, finds the structural vulnerability underneath it, and waits.

Thursday, Aug. 6, he moved into two new targets. And the framing he used tells you exactly how he is thinking about the Artificial Intelligence (AI) infrastructure trade right now.

Burry disclosed a short position in Oracle (ORCL) at $144.63 per share and a larger short exposure in Nebius Group (NBIS) at $211.77, pointing out growing leverage risks tied to off-balance-sheet commitments across the tech and cloud sectors. 

According to a Substack post, He described companies carrying long-term lease obligations that dwarf their current revenue metrics as "very fat, very large, easy to shoot" fish.

ORCL is down 25.68% year-to-date and 43.41% over the past year, according to Yahoo Finance.

NBIS is up 126.84% year-to-date and 244.67% over the past year. Burry is shorting the loser and the winner simultaneously. This is the interesting part of this disclosure.

Also Read: Michael Burry Latest News and Stories

The off-balance-sheet argument Burry is making

Burry's bear case is not actually about revenue or product quality. It is about the liability structure.

Many cloud and AI infrastructure companies carry enormous lease obligations for data center space, power contracts, and compute capacity that do not appear prominently on the income statement but represent multi-year committed cash outflows. 

When demand for AI infrastructure outpaces supply, those commitments look like competitive advantages. When the supply cycle turns, they become fixed costs against declining revenue.

  • Michael Burry increases his bet against popular chip giant

  • Warren Buffett reveals he broke his own investing pattern

  • Mark Cuban bets on MLB with Athletics minority stake

Burry's thesis, as I read it across his recent disclosures, is that the AI infrastructure build-out has pulled forward years of demand into a compressed window. 

The companies that signed 10-year data center leases and committed billions in GPU capacity at 2025 and 2026 prices to meet 2026 demand may find themselves over-leveraged when the cycle moderates.

He has made this argument across semiconductor equipment, memory chips, and now enterprise cloud. Oracle and Nebius represent two very different positions on the AI infrastructure spectrum, which is why both appearing in the same short book is the revealing detail.

content_html_zh:
Michael Burry 最近一直在撰写简短的半导体书籍。 我平仓了他的 Micron 空头头寸、他的 Caterpillar 赌注以及他的 SOXX 头寸。 他的模式一直是一致的。

他首先确定了市场认为无误的叙述，找到其背后的结构性脆弱性，然后等待。

8 月 6 日星期四，他转向了两个新目标。 他使用的框架准确地告诉你他现在如何看待人工智能（AI）基础设施贸易。

Burry 披露了甲骨文 (ORCL) 的空头头寸，每股 144.63 美元，以及 Nebius Group (NBIS) 的较大空头头寸，每股 211.77 美元，并指出与科技和云行业的表外承诺相关的杠杆风险不断增加。

根据 Substack 的一篇帖子，他将那些承担长期租赁义务的公司描述为“非常肥、非常大、容易射杀”的鱼，这些公司目前的收入指标相形见绌。

根据雅虎财经的数据，ORCL 今年迄今下跌了 25.68%，去年下跌了 43.41%。

NBIS 今年迄今上涨 126.84%，去年上涨 244.67%。 伯里同时做空输家和赢家。 这是本次披露的有趣部分。

另请阅读：迈克尔·伯里最新新闻和故事

伯里提出的资产负债表外论点

伯里的悲观理由实际上与收入或产品质量无关。 这是关于责任结构的。

许多云和人工智能基础设施公司对数据中心空间、电力合同和计算能力承担着巨大的租赁义务，这些义务在损益表上并不突出，但代表了多年承诺的现金流出。

当人工智能基础设施的需求超过供应时，这些承诺看起来就像是竞争优势。 当供应周期转变时，它们就变成了固定成本，以应对收入下降。

更多经理买入/卖出：

  • 迈克尔·伯里（Michael Burry）增加了对流行芯片巨头的赌注
  • 沃伦·巴菲特透露他打破了自己的投资模式
  • 马克·库班以田径队少数股权押注美国职业棒球大联盟

正如我在伯里最近披露的信息中读到的那样，他的论点是，人工智能基础设施的建设已经将多年的需求拉入了一个压缩的窗口。

当经济周期放缓时，那些签署了 10 年期数据中心租约并承诺以 2025 年和 2026 年价格提供数十亿 GPU 容量以满足 2026 年需求的公司可能会发现自己杠杆率过高。

他在半导体设备、存储芯片以及现在的企业云领域都提出了这一论点。 Oracle 和 Nebius 代表了人工智能基础设施领域的两种截然不同的立场，这就是为什么两者出现在同一本小书中是揭示细节的原因。
